advances: Explicit selected center and quantitative dimension-only cutoff for one small endpoint and two equal-volume simplex fibers. The gap is a fixed standard-simplex integral over a compact set of directions.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The lifted convex hull has exactly the three stated integer fibers. At either exposed endpoint only that endpoint is used; every combination at zero lies in $B$ by the inclusion of endpoint midpoints and convexity of $B$. The common continuous affine map changes each volume by the same Jacobian and preserves the cap family. In the standard frame choose $p_0\in A$ and shear by $x\mapsto x+zp_0$, so that $0\in A$ and the midpoint inclusion is preserved. Then $C\subset2B$, and $A\subset2(B-B)$ by fixing a point of $C$. Every point of all three fibers has norm at most $R$ since $B$ lies in the unit ball and has diameter $\sqrt2\le\sqrt d$. Now $V=1/d!$ and $1\le|\nabla\lambda_i|\le\sqrt d$.

For any $p\in A$, the simplex $(p+C)/2\subset B$ has volume $2^{-d}V$. The barycentric matrix of its vertices is column stochastic and nonnegative, and its determinant in absolute value is the volume ratio $2^{-d}$. Indeed the barycentric matrix acts on the affine hyperplane of coordinate sum one and on its parallel linear subspace of coordinate sum zero, and acts identically on the quotient by that subspace. Order its row maxima $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_N$. Replace the first row by the sum of all rows (the ones row), and for each $i\ge2$ subtract $q_i/2$ times that row from row $i$. The absolute determinant is unchanged. Hadamard gives
$$
2^{-(N-1)}\le N^{N/2}2^{-(N-1)}\prod_{i=2}^Nq_i
\le N^{N/2}2^{-(N-1)}q_J^{N-J+1},
$$
because $J\ge2$ and all row maxima are at most one. Hence $q_J\ge b+\delta$, using $N-J+1=\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1$. The exponent defining $b+\delta$ has absolute value less than one, so $\delta>0$. The unordered maxima are $(\lambda_i(p)+\max_C\lambda_i)/2$. Each $p$ lies in at least $J$ of the sets defining $c_i$, giving $0\le c_i\le a$ and $\bar c\ge(J/N)a$. The same midpoint inclusion gives $\operatorname{width}_C\lambda_i\le2$.

Write $r=a/V$. The chosen barycentric coordinates sum to one and differ from $b$ by at most $r/(N\Gamma)$. Since $r\le\Gamma/(4d)$ they are positive. Also $|y-g|\le\sqrt d\,r/(N\Gamma)$. For the uniform endpoint credit, fix $|u-\theta_i|\le\eta$ and rescale the affine functional to $F=\lambda_i+v\cdot x$ with $|v|\le\delta/(24R)$. Put $H=\max_C F$, $W=\operatorname{width}_C F$, and $\kappa=R|v|$. The cap $F\ge H-Wr^{1/d}$ contains a homothetic copy of $C$ of volume $a$ about an $F$-maximizer. At any shared base tilt, either the $C$ cap already pays $a$, or its threshold is strictly greater than $H-Wr^{1/d}$ and the $A$ threshold is less than $2F(y)-H+Wr^{1/d}$. For $p$ in the set defining $c_i$, boundedness and the first two radius conditions give
$$
F(p)+H\ge2b+\delta-2\kappa,\quad
F(y)\le b+\delta/8+\kappa,\quad W\le2+2\kappa,\quad r^{1/d}\le\delta/8.
$$
Since $r<1$, subtraction gives $F(p)+H-2F(y)-Wr^{1/d}\ge\delta-\delta/4-\delta/4-6\kappa\ge\delta/4>0$. Thus the endpoints jointly pay at least $c_i$ for every tilt in this angular neighborhood.

The same angular condition and $r\le\Gamma/(4d)$ imply that every vertex $v_k$ of $B$ other than $v_i$ is strictly below the through-$y$ cut with continuous normal $u$. Its value in the reference cut through $g$ with normal $\theta_i$ is $-1/(N|\nabla\lambda_i|)$. The absolute perturbation is at most $\eta|v_k-y|+|y-g|\le\sqrt2/(8N\sqrt d)+1/(4N\sqrt d)<1/(2N\sqrt d)$. The remaining vertex is positive because the barycentric average of all values is zero and every weight is positive. If $\alpha_k$ are the affine values at the vertices, the retained corner has edge ratios $t_k=\alpha_i/(\alpha_i-\alpha_k)$ for $k\ne i$. The barycentric identity yields $\sum_{k\ne i}\lambda_k(y)/t_k=1$. AM–GM gives $\prod_{k\ne i}t_k\ge d^d\prod_{k\ne i}\lambda_k(y)$. Thus the middle cap has volume at least $\Gamma V\prod_{k\ne i}(1+s_k)$ with $s_k=N(\lambda_k(y)-b)$.

Here $\sum_k s_k=0$, $|s_k|\le r/\Gamma\le1$ and all product terms of degree at least two have total absolute value at most $E_d(r/\Gamma)^2$. The middle contribution is therefore at least $\Gamma V-(c_i-\bar c)-(E_d/\Gamma)a^2/V$. Adding the endpoint credit yields at least
$$
\Gamma V+(J/N)a-(E_d/\Gamma)a^2/V.
$$
Since $k_d>0$ and $r\le\Gamma k_d/(2E_d)$, this is at least $\Gamma(V+a/2)+k_da/2$.

For all other unit normals, use the ordinary single-centroid-cap inequality and equality case recorded in the proof of ea91e021ff1f4416. For the standard simplex equality requires the apex-side direction with cutting plane parallel to the opposite facet, exactly one of the $\theta_i$. Centroid cap volume is continuous in the unit normal by dominated convergence off the boundary hyperplane. The compact set in the definition of $G_d$ excludes all equality directions and is nonempty: $-e_1$ is at distance at least $\sqrt{2-2/\sqrt d}>\eta$ from every $\theta_i$. Thus $G_d>0$. Every section of $B$ by a hyperplane has $(d-1)$-area at most $\omega_{d-1}$, since $B$ lies in the unit ball. Moving a threshold by $|u\cdot(y-g)|$ changes normalized cap mass by at most $d!\omega_{d-1}|y-g|$. The middle contribution is consequently at least
$$
V[\Gamma+G_d-d!\omega_{d-1}\sqrt d\,r/(N\Gamma)].
$$
By $r\le G_d/(2Q_d)$ this exceeds $\Gamma(V+a/2)$. This leaves no nonzero continuous direction untested, and both direction estimates hold for every tilt.

A pure-base through-cap has mass $2V$ or $V+a$ since it includes the full middle fiber. Both dominate the target, using $r<1$ and $\Gamma\le1/2$. Tightening any containing cap to a through-cap can only reduce its mass. The common transformations preserve the actual fiber incidence and relative volumes, proving the result in the original frame.
statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $A,B,C$ be compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, with $B,C$ simplices, $|B|=|C|=V>0$, $|A|=a>0$ and $(A+C)/2\subset B$. Lift these fibers to $-1,0,1$ and use summed fiber volume. Normalize by a common affine change sending $B$ to the standard simplex and by a base shear putting $0\in A$. Let $N=d+1$, $b=1/N$, $J=\lceil N/2\rceil$, $R=2\sqrt d$, $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$, and
$$
\delta=N^{-N/[2(\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1)]}-b.
$$
Use the barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$ of the standard simplex, and write
$$
c_i=|\{p\in A:\lambda_i(p)+\max_C\lambda_i\ge2b+\delta\}|,\qquad
\bar c=\frac1N\sum_i c_i.
$$
Here all volumes in the formulas use the normalized frame. Define $y$ by $\lambda_i(y)=b+(c_i-\bar c)/(N\Gamma V)$. With $g$ the centroid of $B$ and $\theta_i=\nabla\lambda_i/|\nabla\lambda_i|$, put
$$
\begin{gathered}
\eta=\min\{\delta/(24R\sqrt d),\,1/(8N\sqrt d)\},\qquad
G_d=\min_{\substack{|u|=1\\\min_i|u-\theta_i|\ge\eta}}
 \left(\frac{|B\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge0\}|}{V}-\Gamma\right),\\
E_d=2^d-d-1,\qquad k_d=J/N-\Gamma/2,\qquad
Q_d=d!\omega_{d-1}\sqrt d/(N\Gamma)+\Gamma/2,
\end{gathered}
$$
where $\omega_{d-1}$ is the unit $(d-1)$-ball volume. Then $G_d>0$ and
$$
0<a/V\le\min\{(\delta/8)^d,\,N\Gamma\delta/8,\,\Gamma/(4d),\,
                     \Gamma k_d/(2E_d),\,G_d/(2Q_d)\}
$$
implies $y\in\operatorname{int} B$ and raw depth at $(0,y)$ at least $\Gamma(V+a/2)$ over every closed ambient halfspace containing that point. The bound scales back to the original frame.
title: Explicit endpoint-credit center for two equal-volume simplex fibers
